title.value: A slide with far too much text

body.value: The explanatory text on this slide is deliberately written far too long, long enough to exceed the density limit the layout declares, so that the density check is certain to catch it. The explanatory text on this slide is deliberately written far too long, long enough to exceed the density limit the layout declares.

items: The first piece of evidence is also written at great length, stretching the sentence on and on so that the total character count climbs past the limit of two hundred and sixty units, until it reads like a paragraph rather than a bullet

The second piece of evidence is just as long-winded, describing the same thing several times over to pile up characters beyond the limit, and then adding a few more meaningless qualifiers for good measure

The third piece of evidence adds a few more words to make sure the slide's total character count really does exceed the density the layout allows, and pushes the line count past what the element box can hold
The fourth piece of evidence keeps stacking up, so that the text overflows the element box and trips the density rule at the same time; this is a deliberately bad example
The fifth piece of evidence exists only for the line count; the content does not matter, what matters is that it pushes the list higher than two hundred and eighty pixels
The sixth piece of evidence is the final blow: both the character count and the height are certainly over the limit here
